stemMarkdown: A boat's speed in still water is 15 km/h. If it takes the same time to travel 45 km downstream as it does to travel 30 km upstream, what is the speed of the stream?
solutionMarkdown: Let the speed of the stream be \(x\) km/h. Then, the downstream speed is \(15 + x\) and the upstream speed is \(15 - x\). The time taken to travel 45 km downstream equals the time to travel 30 km upstream, so we have: $$\frac{45}{15+x} = \frac{30}{15-x}$$. Solving this equation gives \(x=3\) km/h.
altSolutionMarkdown: Using the ratio of distances (45/30), we can set up a direct proportion with speeds to solve for the stream speed \(x\): $$\frac{45}{15+x} = \frac{30}{15-x}$$. Solving this directly gives us \(x=3\) km/h.
